title: Jewish Literacy Foundations
description: A first integrated sequence for independent beginners: source, practice, argument, character, history, and responsible comparison.

units.title: A question opens the page
units.translation: From when do we recite Shema in the evening?
units.prompt: What job does the opening word perform?
choices: It asks for a starting time.
It announces a final ruling.
It names a speaker.
units.explanation: A question word signals that the source is opening an inquiry.

units.title: Hear, Israel
units.hebrew: שמע ישראל ה׳ אלהינו ה׳ אחד
units.translation: Hear, Israel: the Lord is our God, the Lord is one.
units.prompt: What is the strongest first observation?
choices: It directly addresses Israel and makes an affirmation about God.
It settles every later debate about prayer.
It is a Gemara objection.
units.explanation: Start by hearing a source in its own setting before tracing later reception.

units.title: A verse becomes a practice
units.hebrew: שמע ישראל ה׳ אלהינו ה׳ אחד
units.translation: Hear, Israel: the Lord is our God, the Lord is one.
units.prompt: What changes when this verse is encountered in the Siddur?
choices: It stops being a Torah verse.
Its liturgical setting gives it a recurring communal function.
Its words no longer need interpretation.
units.explanation: A later setting adds a function without erasing the source's original voice.

units.title: Trace a command into practice
units.translation: You shall eat, be satisfied, and bless.
units.prompt: What is a responsible way to study this source chain?
choices: Notice how later sources frame the verse for a particular question.
Use the verse alone to decide every personal case.
Skip all intervening sources.
units.explanation: Halakhic literacy follows reception and reasoning across sources; it is not personal psak.

units.title: Name the claim
units.translation: Know today and bring it back to your heart.
units.prompt: Which is a claim rather than merely a topic?
choices: The topic is religion.
Knowledge should be brought into one's inner life.
The verse has Hebrew words.
units.explanation: A claim says something that can be interpreted, supported, and questioned.

units.title: The kind of person who learns
units.hebrew: במקום שאין אנשים השתדל להיות איש
units.translation: Where there are no people acting humanely, strive to be a person.
units.prompt: What is the most careful application?
choices: It invites responsibility when others fail to take it up.
It gives a binding ruling for every emergency.
It requires studying alone forever.
units.explanation: A conceptual application frames practice without pretending to issue a ruling.

units.title: Context and comparison
units.translation: Seek the welfare of the city.
units.prompt: Which question opens a responsible reading?
choices: Which modern view does it automatically settle?
Who is addressed, in what setting, and for what purpose?
How many letters are in the verse?
units.explanation: Context helps us read responsibly; it does not make a source irrelevant.
